correctness.rationale: For every nonempty proper row subset of F_10, published ACM/Achanta results require uniform distribution modulo divisors and preserve full spark under affine units/translations and complement. Independently enumerating uniformly distributed subsets of sizes 1,...,5 found counts 10,20,60,30,20 and the exact affine representatives {0};{0,1};{0,1,2},{0,1,3};{0,1,2,3},{0,1,3,4};{0,1,2,3,4}. Consecutive reps are Vandermonde full spark. For {0,1,3} every 3-column determinant is Vandermonde times x1+x2+x3: three tenth roots cannot sum to zero because primitive cube-root ratios are not tenth roots. The 4-row exceptional representative has a singular minor on columns {0,1,2,6}; independently reduced that determinant to zero modulo Phi_10(z). Ten affine images are bad in size 4, and complements give ten bad in size 6. Full finite domain covered without floating-point zero tests; remaining adjacent sizes 1,2,3,5 and complements full spark.

originality.rationale: Alexeev--Cahill--Mixon Theorem 9 supplies uniformity necessity, invariances and the exact N=10 exceptional singular minor, but not the complete classification of EVERY uniform row set at N=10. Achanta et al give coprime/single-missing-row criteria and revisit the same counterexample, yet do not enumerate or classify all affine row orbits at N=10. The finite exhaustive orbit theorem is an additional natural exact classification, although much of its ingredients are published; no dominating exact table was located.
residual_risks: The new proof leverages published N=10 counterexample and substantial known affine/complement reductions; some exact finite census may be folklore or an appendix not indexed.
The statement is limited to Fourier order 10 and not a general composite-order criterion.
